tor_001: You can recognise it by its heavy fluted trunk, over 6 metres round, and in summer by green seed chains up to half a metre long. It stands at the centre of the Giardino Sambuy in Piazza Carlo Felice.
tor_002: You can recognise it by its huge crown, about 30 metres across, covering most of the garden, and its flaking camouflage bark. It stands in the Giardini Cavour on Piazza Cavour.
tor_003: You can recognise it by its straight trunk, limbs coming off in level tiers, and fan-shaped leaves that turn hard yellow in November. It stands about 60 metres from the plane in the Giardini Cavour.
tor_004: You can recognise it by its wide, even dome of a crown, standing alone on open grass with room on every side. It stands at the northern end of Parco del Valentino, near Corso Massimo d'Azeglio.
tor_005: You can recognise it by its short, heavy trunk and limbs reaching out almost horizontally, the shape an oak takes with open space around it. It stands behind the Castello del Valentino, near the Rocaille.
tor_006: You can recognise it by its very thick trunk, 6 metres round, grown wide and sideways rather than tall, with bark like a jigsaw of grey, olive and cream. It stands on Viale Virgilio opposite the Eridano.
tor_007: You can recognise it by its great height, 36 metres, towering directly behind the low timber and stone rooftops of the Borgo Medievale. It stands on Viale Virgilio in Parco del Valentino.
tor_008: You can recognise it by its height, 40 metres, the tallest tree in Turin, with the widest canopy on the register, 32 metres across. It stands beside the Fontana dei Dodici Mesi.
tor_009: You can recognise it by its trunk, 6.65 metres round, the widest on Turin's whole register, with a crown so wide it dominates the park. It stands in Parco della Tesoriera on Corso Francia.
tor_010: You can recognise it by its short trunk splitting into dozens of near-vertical stems, a vase shape rather than a dome, orange-brown in autumn. It stands in the Giardini Reali Inferiori on Piazza Castello.
